data.narrative:
Flamefront Propulsion is a pre-seed stage company in the Defense & Security sector, founded by Matt Garcia (MIT aeronautical background, former founding engineer and head of propulsion at Mach Industries). The addressable peer universe comprises 26 same-sector companies, of which 2 are public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 are private. Top private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Castelion, Shield AI, and Saronic.

A peer-median valuation approach is not applicable here. The screen for same-stage or adjacent-stage peers within Defense & Security yielded insufficient data—zero same-stage matches and only one adjacent-stage match—falling short of the minimum three-datapoint threshold required for reliable triangulation. Reliance on a broader all-sector median would introduce material bias and obscure sector-specific dynamics. The public comparable set of two companies is similarly sparse for statistical anchoring.

Given these constraints, traditional comparable company methodology cannot responsibly support a point estimate. The analysis instead establishes that any valuation framework must account for (1) founder pedigree and propulsion domain expertise as a key value signal; (2) the early-stage, pre-revenue nature of the business, which limits financial-metric anchoring; and (3) the concentration of private capital in adjacent defense-tech ventures at higher maturity stages. A credible range would require either direct investor market signals or forward-looking technical and commercial milestones as primary drivers rather than peer-based multiples.
